newsitem.title: HONG KONG: UN has no role monitoring Hong Kong rights-Annan.
newsitem.headline: UN has no role monitoring Hong Kong rights-Annan.

text.p: The United Nations has no role monitoring human or political rights in Hong Kong after the territory's handover from Britain to China at midnight on Monday, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said.
He said the 1984 Joint Declaration between Britain and China governing Hong Kong's handover left no room for United Nations involvement.
"The instruments are deposited with us but the agreement gives us no role," Annan told reporters in Hong Kong hours before the handover. "The agreement doesn't give us a monitoring role."

Democratic activists in Hong Kong and around the world have expressed concern that Beijing will restrict personal and press freedoms here despite pledging to preserve the territory's unique way of life for 50 years after the handover.
The activists point to Beijing's dismissal of Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council and its replacement by an appointed Provisional Legislature as proof of China's intentions.
Asked whether the territory's future was a legitimate international issue, Annan said:
"I think that China would be within its rights to argue that it is an internal matter."
Annan said the lack of any formal United Nations role in Hong Kong did not mean that as Secretary-General he would be indifferent to post-handover rights problems.
"If there were to be a real need and there was a compelling human rights or humanitarian abuse, yes, I have spoken up and I do speak when this occurs," he said.
China is rolling back some key political freedoms in Hong Kong to reverse reforms it says were introduced without its consent in the twilight years of British rule.
